title: Harbhagat Names Taru Singh of Poolha

blocks.text: The nawab now demands names, ordering his men to identify those who send provisions to the Singhs so they can be destroyed as examples. Harbhagat Niranjania answers by turning suspicion into accusation and directing state violence toward specific Sikh householders.

He points to Taru Singh of village Poolha, describing a cultivator who pays what is due, keeps only a little for himself, and sends the remainder onward to the Khalsa. Taru Singh is thus portrayed not as a rebel sustained by wealth, but as a village Sikh who converts ordinary labor into support for a persecuted community.

The page widens that portrait by bringing in Taru Singh's mother and sister, who live austerely, reject rival devotional claims, and move supplies discreetly toward the Singhs; it then introduces Mehtab Singh as another dangerous supporter living more openly in militant fashion. Together these details explain why the state begins to pursue Taru Singh's household with special determination.
